messages.subject: interpretation of multiple group analysis results
parts:
Hi, I conducted multiple group analysis under graded response model and compared the pairs of models via the anova() function as below:
anova(mod_metric_grm, mod_configural_grm)
anova(mod_scalar2_grm, mod_metric_grm)
anova(mod_scalar1_grm, mod_scalar2_grm)
anova(mod_fullconstrain_grm, mod_scalar1_grm)
anova(mod_scalar1_grm, mod_fullconstrain_grm)

Then, I got the results below:

anova(mod_metric_grm, mod_configural_grm) AIC SABIC HQ BIC logLik X2 df p mod_metric_grm 1085079 1086386 1085810 1087295 -542253.7 mod_configural_grm 1084997 1086422 1085794 1087413 -542186.5 134.491 26 0 > anova(mod_scalar2_grm, mod_metric_grm) AIC SABIC HQ BIC logLik X2 df p mod_scalar2_grm 1086330 1087051 1086733 1087554 -543006.9 mod_metric_grm 1085079 1086386 1085810 1087295 -542253.7 1506.307 128 0 > anova(mod_scalar1_grm, mod_scalar2_grm) AIC SABIC HQ BIC logLik X2 df p mod_scalar1_grm 1086400 1087117 1086801 1087616 -543043.0 mod_scalar2_grm 1086330 1087051 1086733 1087554 -543006.9 72.241 1 0 > anova(mod_fullconstrain_grm, mod_scalar1_grm) AIC SABIC HQ BIC logLik X2 df p mod_fullconstrain_grm 1086431 1087143 1086829 1087639 -543059.4 mod_scalar1_grm 1086400 1087117 1086801 1087616 -543043.0 32.787 1 0 > anova(mod_scalar1_grm, mod_fullconstrain_grm) AIC SABIC HQ BIC logLik X2 df p mod_scalar1_grm 1086400 1087117 1086801 1087616 -543043.0 mod_fullconstrain_grm 1086431 1087143 1086829 1087639 -543059.4 -32.787 -1 NaN


>

However, I am confused about the selecting the best model fitting the data. How can I decide the best model?
Is there any article or material I can benefit for the interpretation of the resuls?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: interpretation of multiple group analysis results
parts:
"Best fitting" is difficult to tell in this context, though these fit statistics are based on how well the model will likely perform if a new sample were drawn and compared. Lower information criteria are generally preferred, where if your sample size is reasonably large (as it look to be here) then you could pick the model with the lowest AIC and continue with that one. Of course, you'll want to inspect other things like itemfit and (global) model fit, but it's a start. HTH.

Phil
